openings.claim: Locating the earliest supported divergence need not depend on reconstructing chronological order from local timestamps.
openings.delta: Remove timestamp sorting as the ordering dependency. Compare recorded input/output boundaries in manifest stage order; carry record identifiers into a ledger. Report the first supported mismatch, or an unresolved interval wherever missing or incomparable boundaries prevent localization. Keep timestamp anomalies as observations, without inferring execution or cause.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, ordinary timestamp-first review, the stipulated early export timestamp will not place export before parse. Missing transform outputs or removed transform records will produce explicit localization uncertainty rather than evidence of nonexecution. This predicts differing ordering and interval decisions, not reliable recovery of injected causes; a rival that already treats timestamps as uncertain may agree.
openings.probe: Pilot only: inspect each available record at most once, with twelve total manual inspections per pair shared between variants. A local script applies manifest-first and timestamp-first ordering to that same captured ledger across both disjoint three-pair subsets. Freeze referenced claims and intervals before opening either answer sheet. Compare supported-stage accuracy and whether intervals contain supplied injected boundaries; then mask the stipulated removed transform records and inspect interval changes without additional manual reads. Use sixty minutes for capture/output and twenty for comparison. Reusing one capture and sorting four stages makes this a bounded comparison, although completion time is unproved.
assumptions: Dictionary definitions permit comparison at corresponding artifact boundaries; otherwise return unresolved.
Manifest order supplies expected structural sequence, not proof that any listed stage executed.
Defeated as a discriminating opening if both variants already discount timestamps and yield identical claims/intervals. Invalid boundary matching defeats definite localization.

Answer-sheet coverage bounds scoring; missing coverage or exhausted analyst capacity leaves evaluation unresolved. Successful scoring cannot establish the converse that chronological reconstruction is always unnecessary.

assessment: One removal candidate preserves the reporting contract through explicit uncertainty. Expected order and recorded mismatches support review decisions; causal explanations remain hypotheses.
